reason: The hypothesis directly applies the Y2O3 nanoparticle addition strategy from P17 and P19, which already demonstrated grain refinement and strength improvement in NiCoCr-based superalloys and MPEAs, to a Ti- and Ni-rich HEA system (Ni-Co-Fe-Cr-Al-Ti) studied in P1 and P41. The mechanism, intervention, and predicted outcome are taken almost verbatim from these sources, and the proposal merely substitutes the base alloy without introducing a new mechanistic insight or resolving a conflict between passages.
copied_elements: Adding 0.5 wt.% Y2O3 nanoparticles to refine grains and improve strength (P17, P19)
Grain boundary pinning and dislocation obstruction by nanoparticles (P17, P19, P33)
Enhanced yield strength and ductility at high temperature (P17, P19, P34)
Application to Ni-Co-Cr-based alloy processed by additive manufacturing (P17, P19)
Use of directed energy deposition for Ni-Co-Fe-Cr-Al-Ti HEA (P1, P41)
